\subsection{Negative Binomial}

NiMARE's negative binomial uses shape $r=s_1^2/(\theta s_2)$ and success
probability $\pi_v=(1+s_1/(\theta u_v s_2))^{-1}$. Writing $\eta=\log s_1$ and
$\kappa=\log k$ with $k=\theta s_2/s_1^2$, the voxel mean is $\mu_v=e^\eta u_v$, the size is
$1/k$, and each voxel's summand depends on $(\eta,\kappa)$ and $S_v$ alone. Below,
$x_v=k\mu_v$.


\noindent The expressions the claims are formed from:

\begin{equation*}
  \lambda(\eta, \kappa, S_v) = \kappa y + y \log{\left(e^{S} e^{\eta} \right)} - \left(y + e^{- \kappa}\right) \log{\left(e^{S} e^{\eta} e^{\kappa} + 1 \right)} + \operatorname{loggamma}{\left(y + e^{- \kappa} \right)} - \operatorname{loggamma}{\left(e^{- \kappa} \right)}
\end{equation*}
\noindent One voxel's log-likelihood, up to $-\log\Gamma(Y_v+1)$.

\begin{equation*}
  G_1 = y - \left(\operatorname{polygamma}{\left(0,y + e^{- \kappa} \right)} - \operatorname{polygamma}{\left(0,e^{- \kappa} \right)}\right) e^{- \kappa}
\end{equation*}
\noindent The count term of $\lambda_\kappa$. $\operatorname{polygamma}(0, \cdot)$ is the digamma function.

\begin{equation*}
  G_2 = \left(\operatorname{polygamma}{\left(0,y + e^{- \kappa} \right)} - \operatorname{polygamma}{\left(0,e^{- \kappa} \right)}\right) e^{- \kappa} + \left(\operatorname{polygamma}{\left(1,y + e^{- \kappa} \right)} - \operatorname{polygamma}{\left(1,e^{- \kappa} \right)}\right) e^{- 2 \kappa}
\end{equation*}
\noindent The count term of $\lambda_{\kappa\kappa}$.

\begin{equation*}
  g(x_v) = - \frac{1}{x_{v} + 1} + \frac{\log{\left(x_{v} + 1 \right)}}{x_{v}}
\end{equation*}
